subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - burst capacity & scale-up times
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fastpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@fastpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - burst capacity & scale-up times

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can get to an action plan. High-level FastPay requirements: 

- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end (first-token for streaming scenarios) <= 200ms for low-latency chat path; p99 <= 500ms for non-streaming/batch.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline steady-state ~300 req/s with typical concurrency of ~80 concurrent active sessions; spikes up to ~900 req/s during peak events.
- Streaming: we need token-by-token streaming for user-facing chat. First-byte (initial partial reply) should be < 150ms p50, but p95 goal is the p95 end-to-end above.
- Autoscale/burst behavior: must handle bursts to ~3x baseline. Preferred scale-up time for critical path <= 60s; acceptable up to 90s if warm pool semantics guaranteed (i.e., new replicas can accept traffic immediately with no cold-start token penalty). Queueing: short queuing window allowed (<= 10s) for burst handling but would prefer < 5s.

Open questions we flagged:
1) How you would model warm pools vs. cold start behavior and expected first-token penalty in each case.
2) Whether Redwood can provide a configurable warm-pool of reserved GPUs and what the cost delta looks like.
3) Fallback behaviors (e.g., model variant with reduced context length) and how that affects quality.

Next steps from our side: Jamal and I will share an internal traffic trace and a sample SLO spreadsheet (attached). Please confirm you can meet the p95 numbers with the proposed autoscale config or suggest an alternative with clear tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Director of Platform Engineering, FastPay

Attachment: slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 targets by route and time windows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fastpay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - burst capacity & scale-up times

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the SLO spreadsheet. Appreciate the specifics; that makes it easier to propose a concrete approach. High level response and proposed next steps below.

High-level approach we recommend:
- Dedicated warm pool: we can provision a small reserved pool (warm replicas) pinned to your account to reduce first-token cold start. Typical warm-pool sizing for 3x burst-to-baseline is 25-30% of the peak burst capacity.
- Scale-up policy: a staged scale from warm pool -> reserved burst replicas -> autoscale to public capacity. We can aim for effective scale-to-capacity within ~45s for requests routed to warm replicas, and up to ~90s for cold-started public capacity.
- Queueing behavior: we can configure short FIFO queueing with a 30s TTL for requests during burst; we recommend a soft limit target of < 5s average wait for critical routes.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model variant for non-critical paths to reduce latency under heavy load; this is configurable per-route.

Technical ask for our engineering follow-up (Dev): can you prepare an initial capacity profile (GPU types, expected tokens/sec per GPU, batching, typical sequence lengths) and a proposed autoscale config (min warm replicas, burst target, scale-up thresholds)? Please include expected first-token penalty numbers for cold vs warm replicas. Also attaching a diagram (autoscale-architecture-diagram.png) to show the proposed flow.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Dev to provide technical capacity proposal (ETA: 2027-04-21 EOD).
2) Redwood to run a small load-validation plan (joint test) once we have your traffic trace (you mentioned you'd share).
3) Pricing + draft SLA to follow after validation (we'll attach a proposal).

If that works we'll schedule a short technical sync for Thursday to walk the proposal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Tel: (415) 555-0123

Attachment: autoscale-architecture-diagram.png (diagram of warm pool -> burst -> fallback routing)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fastpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Autoscale SLO qualification - burst capacity & scale-up times

Hi Sarah — following up with the technical proposal Marissa requested. I built this against the traffic profile you shared (thanks). TL;DR: feasible with a dedicated warm pool + modest burst reserves and a fallback plan. Details below.

Assumptions from trace:
- Baseline: 300 req/s (avg), typical concurrency ~80 active sessions.
- Peak bursts: up to ~900 req/s for short windows (2-8 minutes).
- Average sequence length: 40 tokens; streaming enabled; median tokens/sec per request ~5.

Proposed serving config:
1) Instance sizing: recommend NVIDIA-A10x GPUs for cost/throughput balance for your models (we'll calibrate on your exact model weights). Estimated throughput per A10x for streaming/chat workloads: ~80-120 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU (depends on batching).
2) Warm pool: min_reserved_replicas = 4 (covers ~320 concurrent streaming sessions), sized to cover ~1.0-1.5x baseline steady-state. Warm replicas are pinned and pre-warmed (model loaded, KV cache warmed for recent prefixes if desired). Expected first-token penalty on warm replica: ~10-30ms (model load already done).
3) Burst reserve policy: reserved_burst_replicas = 6 -> can absorb additional ~480 concurrent sessions quickly (target route-to-ready within 30-45s). These replicas are kept in a warm start snapshot and can accept traffic with minimal initialization.
4) Autoscale to public capacity: additional capacity spun from shared pool if burst exceeds reserved_burst_replicas; expected cold-start first-token penalty ~800-1200ms on first traffic for a new replica (model load), but subsequent requests normal.
5) Queueing and throttling: configure per-route FIFO queue with 30s TTL. We suggest an adaptive shed policy: if queue wait > 10s, route to reduced-quality model variant (quantized) with lower latency.
6) Batching: continuous batching for non-streaming endpoints; for streaming endpoints we limit batching to preserve first-byte latency — target micro-batches (2-8k tokens) to balance throughput/latency.

Expected latency windows (based on calibration and safety margin):
- Streaming first-byte: warm pool p50 ~40-120ms; p95 ~180-240ms (depends on sequence length and tokenization);
- Non-streaming p95 (end-to-end) on warm pool: ~180-300ms depending on batching;
- Cold public replica first-byte p95: ~1000-1300ms on first request.

Validation plan:
- Joint load test with your traffic trace and 3 synthetic burst profiles (2x, 3x, 5x baseline) to verify p95 windows.
- Run tests with warm pool enabled vs disabled to measure delta and validate our warm-pool sizing.
- Capture telemetry: per-token latencies, queue wait times, CPU/GPU utilization, model load times.

Deliverables: proposal-draft.pdf (attached) with cost estimates for warm pool + reserved burst replicas and a draft SLA language for the burst window.

If the latency p95 ranges above look acceptable, we can schedule a validation run as early as 2027-04-25.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal-draft.pdf (pricing and SLA draft)

Marissa / Dev — this looks good, thanks for the detailed breakdown. A couple quick items:

- The warm-pool + reserved burst model makes sense. We want to confirm the cost delta and get a firm SLA exception for the 45s scale-up SLA when warm pool routing is used.
- Can you include explicit test success criteria in the validation run doc? For example:
  * Test A (2x burst): p95 streaming first-byte <= 200ms for 95% of windows; queue wait < 5s
  * Test B (3x burst): p95 streaming first-byte <= 300ms for 90% of windows; queue wait < 10s
  * Test C (5x burst): graceful degradation to quantized model for non-critical routes with minimal error rate increase

Assuming the validation run meets those criteria, we'll proceed to pricing and legal. Can we schedule a 30-minute call on Monday 2027-04-26 to finalize the validation plan and timeline? Also please add a line item in the proposal for a monthly warm-pool reservation cost and an hourly burst reserve cost.

Thanks — Jamal and I are aligned to move quickly on this.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Director of Platform Engineering, FastPay
